match.reason: Both bank points teach matching one register to the audience and warn that mixing registers sounds out of place, whereas this point teaches deliberately mixing formal and informal language for effect, so no bank point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Choosing the level of formality
card: Formal language uses full sentences, precise words and no slang. It suits speeches, reports and official occasions.
Informal language is relaxed and close to everyday talk. It may use slang, short forms like "we're" and a personal tone.
A speaker can mix the two on purpose. For example, a principal might tell a casual story inside a formal speech.
The informal moment can make the audience feel the speaker is one of them. The formal parts keep the speech serious and credible.
draft.remember: Mixing formal and informal language on purpose can build a connection while keeping a speech credible.

a.q: Why might a speaker add a casual story to a formal speech?
opts: To connect with the audience while staying credible
To show the speaker does not care about the topic
To make the speech sound like a written report
To replace the formal points with everyday talk
a.why: A casual story makes the speaker feel closer to the audience, and the formal parts around it keep the speech serious. It is not a replacement for the formal points, because the card says the two are mixed.
a.clue: Think about what the audience feels when a speaker sounds like one of them.

b.q: Ayesha, a school captain, opens a formal assembly speech on school values with a funny story about losing her bus pass. She then returns to precise, formal language. What is the best explanation of her choice?
opts: She used an informal moment to relate to students
She forgot the speech needed to be formal throughout
She wanted the whole speech to sound like casual chat
She used informal language because the topic is unimportant
b.why: Ayesha's story is a deliberate informal moment that helps students relate to her, and the return to formal language keeps the serious message credible. It is not a mistake, because she moves back to formal language on purpose.
b.clue: She goes back to formal language after the story.

a.best: To connect with the audience while staying credible

b.best: She used an informal moment to relate to students
